requirements.requirement: Web application runs under the unprivileged appsvc account (not root)
requirements.summary: appsvc (uid 1000) was created via useradd; the container/conmon process runs under user-1000.slice cgroup both before and after reboot, and post-reboot ps confirms the main container process (conmon, pid 818) is owned by user appsvc, not root.

requirements.requirement: Application is run as a container
requirements.summary: A rootless Podman Quadlet unit (webapp.container) running nginx:alpine was created and started as a systemd --user service; podman info and container process tree (conmon/crun/nginx) confirm containerized execution.

ss shows a listener on *:8080 (pasta) and curl to both 127.0.0.1:8080 and $NODE_IP:8080 returned HTTP 200 both before and after the reboot; the fixed after-executor listening-sockets snapshot independently confirms port 8080 is bound.

requirements.requirement: Service starts at boot while appsvc has no active login session
requirements.summary: loginctl linger was enabled for appsvc; loginctl list-sessions showed zero sessions both pre- and post-reboot; after the node reboot (new boot_id 0fd74c0c...) webapp.service was already active (started immediately post-boot) with zero login sessions present, directly demonstrating boot-time start without a login session.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (5f3ce3b8...) and healthy state (service active, HTTP 200, zero sessions) captured; systemctl reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id (0fd74c0c...) differs, confirming an actual restart; recovered service/data/cluster state confirmed via active webapp.service, HTTP 200 on both endpoints, and container process owned by appsvc. Fixed before-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots independently corroborate the boot_id transition.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, converging evidence: an unprivileged appsvc account runs a rootless Podman container (nginx:alpine) serving on port 8080, started via a linger-enabled systemd --user Quadlet service with no active login session, both before and after a full node reboot that changed the boot_id (5f3ce3b8... -> 0fd74c0c...) and showed clean recovery of service, HTTP responses, and process ownership. Operational hygiene is high, with only expected reboot-related artifacts observed.
limitations: Reboot polling commands (cmd-d9d50efe7b0d45ee, cmd-12211ed0e67344ec) returned -1 due to expected connection loss during reboot; this is not evidence of task failure but means the exact moment of service auto-start could not be observed mid-transition, only before and after.
No evidence of container image content/HTTP body validation beyond status code 200, so functional correctness of the nginx default page (vs. a custom app) is assumed from status code alone.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 17 chronological executor commands: user creation, podman install, linger enable, quadlet creation, service start/verify, and reboot verification are all directly tied to the task or the mandatory restart protocol. The one failed command (machinectl shell, cmd-68e9c83016244d9b) was a read-only diagnostic attempt with no return-code-indicated state change. The three -1 return-code commands around the reboot are expected connection drops/timeouts during the reboot polling window, not failures indicating unwanted mutation. A /tmp/reboot.log file was created as a side effect of the reboot mechanism (nohup redirect); this is a minor, low-risk residue directly tied to the mandated restart step rather than an unnecessary mutation. No abandoned files, conflicting services, unsafe exposure, or damaged package state were observed; failed-services and package-health checks remained clean before and after.
